title: worktree merge: commit the lane rewrite instead of leaving it as dirt
action: Closes the P3 residual the mcl-2 re-judge raised (merge-closes-the-lane D1/D4). Today `close_the_lane_on_merge` runs at the tail of `merge_finish` (verbs/worktree/phases.rs, after the post-commit tracked-files guard has taken its reading) and rewrites `.bee/lanes/<feature>.json` — a TRACKED file in this repo — leaving it modified-but-uncommitted in main. It sits there until some unrelated bookkeeping auto-commit sweeps it up, and until then any OTHER post-commit drift is indistinguishable from it in the operator's tree. Fix: right after the lane rewrite succeeds, make ONE path-scoped commit of exactly that one lane file, so the merge leaves a clean tree. Reuse the existing path-scoped bookkeeping-commit helper the merge path already owns (`commit_main_bookkeeping` and its opt-out key are the precedent — read them and follow their shape rather than inventing a new git invocation): path-scoped `git commit -- <lane path>`, never `git add -A`, never `--amend`. Amending the merge commit was considered and is REJECTED: it rewrites a commit the integration queue has already published as landed, for a bookkeeping row. A second, clearly-named commit solves the actual harm — uncommitted dirt indistinguishable from real drift — without rewriting history. ORDERING, load-bearing: the new commit runs AFTER the post-commit tracked-files guard has already taken its reading. Moving the guard, narrowing it, or exempting a path inside it is out of scope and forbidden (merge-closes-the-lane D4, and the critical pattern docs/knowledge/patterns/20260818-a-write-placed-before-a-self-check-makes-the.md). Best-effort like every other bookkeeping write on this path: a failed commit warns on its own line and the merge stays green.

truths: After a green merge that rewrote the lane, `git status --porcelain` in MAIN reports the lane file as clean — the rewrite is committed, not left as dirt.
The lane rewrite lands in its own path-scoped commit naming only that one lane file; no other path is swept in and the merge commit itself is not amended.
The post-commit tracked-files guard is unchanged — not moved, not narrowed, no path exempted inside it — and still takes its reading before the new commit runs.
A merge that wrote no lane change (already-up-to-date, MERGE_CONFLICT, WORKTREE_MERGE_PROOF_DEBT) creates no extra commit.
A failing lane commit warns on its own line and the merge still returns green.
The regression test keeps its fixture lane file TRACKED, since an untracked one is invisible to both the guard and this behavior.
Every merge test that passed before this cell still passes.

done_when: A green merge leaves MAIN's tree clean with respect to the lane file, the rewrite carried in its own path-scoped commit; the guard is byte-identical; no extra commit appears on the no-op merge paths; a failing commit warns without turning the merge red.
notes: Single cell, single slice. Do not touch verbs/drivers/close.rs or verbs/state_group/** — the lane-write helper and the close driver both stay as shipped.

report.outcome: Lane rewrite from close_the_lane_on_merge now lands in its own path-scoped commit right after the write succeeds, via the existing commit_main_bookkeeping mechanism; a green merge leaves main's tree clean, the merge commit is never amended, and a failed lane commit only warns.
report.tests: PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml worktree — green (186 passed, 0 failed) — scope: cell touches only worktree/phases.rs and worktree/tests.rs, so the worktree test module is the exact and sufficient scope

checks.evidence: phases.rs:644-649 builds a single-element pathspec naming only the merged feature's lane record and hands it to commit_main_bookkeeping, which scopes every step — status, add and commit all carry the same pathspec (merge.rs:271-350, git.rs:118-125). No bare add-all reaches this path. The new test asserts the resulting commit's diff names exactly that one file (tests.rs:3707-3712) and passes.

A search for amend across verbs/worktree returns only comment and doc-string hits; no git invocation carries it, and commit_unsigned hardcodes its argument list (git.rs:119). The test asserts the new commit has one parent while the merge commit below it still carries two (tests.rs:3680-3706).

The revision is purely additive: 110 insertions, zero deletions, a single hunk starting below the guard. The guard block is byte-identical and at the same lines in both trees, still carrying no pathspec and no exemption. The new commit is inserted after both the guard and the lane rewrite.

The call sits inside merge_finish, reachable only from the staged outcome. Already-up-to-date and conflict both return done from merge_stage, and proof debt refuses before the merge runs. Two further guards: the call is nested inside the non-empty next-action arm, and commit_main_bookkeeping reports skipped-clean and commits nothing when its scoped status is empty.

phases.rs:650-656 emits a single warning line on a non-clean skip reason with no return and no error, falling through to the unchanged green result. commit_main_bookkeeping never returns an error shape — every failure arm yields skipped, including an index restore after a failed commit.

The fixture un-ignores the lane directory, force-adds the lane record and commits it, through a helper that asserts success — a failed force-add fails the test rather than passing silently. Proof it is genuinely tracked rather than merely present: the test asserts the file appears in a commit diff, which an ignored untracked file never could.

The test asserts an empty porcelain status through a helper that does NOT pass untracked-files=no, so untracked leftovers would fail it too. The only other tracked-file writer on this path writes the lane record and nothing else.
The revision deletes no line, so no pre-existing test was modified or removed. The worktree module reports 186 passed, 0 failed; the full suite reports 2041 passed, 0 failed.
